name: Evero Ince Bio Power (InBECCS)
capacity_note: 21.5 MWe waste-wood biomass; 170,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Evero Energy press releases 2024-2025; Bioenergy Insight Magazine; UK HyNet Track 1 deliverability assessment Oct 2024
notes: ACTIVE BECCS PROJECT. UK government-approved for HyNet Track 1 CCS retrofit. InBECCS project: 250,000 t CO2/yr capture planned, target operational 2030. CCS via HyNet North West pipeline to Liverpool Bay storage. One of UK's first commercial-scale BECCS plants.

name: Evero Mersey Bio Energy (BECCS)
capacity_note: 20.9 MWe waste-wood biomass; ~150,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Evero Energy press releases 2024; Energy Voice report Oct 2024; Chester Standard report
notes: HyNet Track 1 expansion candidate alongside Ince. Located near Widnes, Cheshire. Both Mersey and Ince plants together process >300,000 t/yr waste wood. CCS retrofit under development through HyNet.

name: Kent Renewable Energy (Sandwich CHP)
capacity_note: 28.1 MWe / 25 MWth biomass CHP; ~210 GWh/yr
source: Kent Renewable Energy Ltd website; Greenvolt acquisition announcement 2024; Bioenergy International; power-technology.com profile
notes: Biomass CHP burning wood chips and agricultural biomass. ~210.8 GWh generated in 2023. Saves ~45,000 t CO2/yr on fossil displacement basis. Located in Pfizer industrial area, Sandwich, Kent. Greenvolt acquisition completed ~Oct 2024.

name: Margam Green Energy (Port Talbot)
capacity_note: 40 MWe waste-wood biomass; 250,000 t/yr waste wood
source: Margam Green Energy website; Generandi/Greencoat acquisition report; Babcock & Wilcox Vølund case study
notes: £160M waste-wood-fired power station; operational since 2019. Processes contaminated waste wood including C&D waste without pre-treatment. Powers ~75,000 homes. O&M by Babcock & Wilcox Vølund. Adjacent to Port Talbot Steelworks site — decarbonisation cluster potential.

name: Sleaford Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 38.5 MWe straw-fired biomass; ~240,000 t/yr straw
source: Global Energy Monitor Sleaford REP entry; power-technology.com profile; BWSC reference page; electricityproduction.uk
notes: Agricultural straw-fired power station. Commissioned September 2014. Located at Eslaford Park, North Kesteven, Lincolnshire. BWSC operates under 15-yr agreement. Straw sourced within 50-mile radius.

name: Snetterton Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 44.2 MWe straw/biomass; ~300,000 t straw per year
source: power-technology.com Snetterton profile; PensionDanmark press release; IPP Journal project record
notes: 44.9 MWe straw-fired biomass plant in Breckland District, Norfolk. Commissioned April 2017. BWSC owner/operator. Saves ~300,000 t CO2 fossil displacement. Part of same UK straw-to-power cluster as Sleaford and Brigg.

name: Brigg Renewable Energy Plant
capacity_note: 40 MWe straw-fired biomass; 240,000 t/yr wheat straw
operator: BWSC North Lincs Ltd (JV: BWSC / PensionDanmark / CIP)
source: power-technology.com Brigg Biomass profile; BWSC reference; Renewables Now news 2016; New Civil Engineer
notes: Straw-fired 40 MWe power station at Glanford Vale Business Park, Scawby Brook, near Brigg, North Lincolnshire. Built on former British Sugar factory site. Commissioned early 2016. 240,000 t/yr wheat straw from within 50-mile radius. 15-yr BWSC O&M contract.

name: Wilton 10 (Sembcorp Teesside Biomass)
capacity_note: 30 MWe / 10 MWth biomass CHP; 300,000 t/yr wood waste
source: Wikipedia: Wilton power stations; power-technology.com Wilton 10 profile; Sembcorp press release 2007
notes: UK's first large-scale commercial wood-to-energy plant (opened Nov 2007). Burns 300,000 t/yr sustainable wood, sawmill waste and wood offcuts. Located within Wilton petrochemical complex — industrial CCS cluster opportunity (HyNet or Teesside cluster). Steam output piped to wider Wilton complex.

name: SELCHP (South East London CHP)
capacity_note: 35 MWe EfW; 460,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: SELCHP; Veolia UK press release (25 years, 2019); SELCHP.com; Southwark Council website
notes: Opened November 1994; one of London's longest-operating EfW plants. Processes 460,000 t/yr; 35 MWe steam turbine. Located at Spa Road, Bermondsey/Deptford. Provides district heating. Biogenic fraction of MSW ~50% (EU average, Eurostat); ~0.21 Mt biogenic CO2/yr estimated (calc: 460,000 t × 0.5 biogenic × 0.9 combustion efficiency × ~1 tCO2/t biogenic waste).

name: Cory Riverside 1 (Belvedere EfW)
capacity_note: 66 MWe EfW; 750,000 t/yr waste
source: Cory Group website; power-technology.com Riverside RRF project; WSP case study; Cory sustainability emissions page
notes: One of Europe's largest single-site EfW plants. 750,000 t/yr capacity; 66 MWe. Cory Decarbonisation Project targets 1.4 Mt CO2 savings/yr from Riverside 1+2 by 2030 via CCS. Adjacent Riverside 2 (650,000 t, 61 MWe) under construction 2026. CCS pathway through Thames Estuary or East Coast cluster.

name: Lakeside EfW (Colnbrook)
capacity_note: 37 MWe EfW; 450,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: Lakeside EfW; Viridor website; Global Energy Monitor Lakeside EfW entry; Wikiwaste Lakeside EfW
notes: JV between Grundon Waste Management and Viridor. Located in Colnbrook, Slough near Heathrow. 450,000 t/yr permitted; 37 MWe. Biogenic CO2 estimated at 50% of combustion CO2 (EU MSW biogenic fraction).

name: Viridor Runcorn EfW
capacity_note: ~100 MWe total EfW (Phase 1+2); 1,100,000 t/yr waste
source: Viridor Runcorn EfW website; Letsrecycle.com capacity extension news; Keppel Seghers Phase 1 commissioning release; Global Energy Monitor Runcorn EfW entry; Viridor CCS project page
notes: UK's largest single-site EfW facility by waste throughput. 1.1 Mt/yr; Phase 1: 425,000 t, 35 MWe + 51 MWth steam. Powers ~211,000 homes equivalent. Viridor actively developing CCS retrofit — Runcorn CCS Project on company website. HyNet North West cluster proximity makes this a high-priority CCS candidate.

name: Severnside Energy Recovery Centre (Avonmouth)
capacity_note: 37 MWe EfW; 400,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikiwaste Severnside ERC; SUEZ UK blog; Global Energy Monitor Avonmouth ERF; PRIVA case study
notes: Waste primarily delivered by rail from West London and Bristol areas. Located adjacent to Seabank Power Station, Avonmouth industrial area. 400,000 t/yr; 37 MWe. Potential future CCS linkage to Portbury/Avonmouth CO2 logistics.

name: Beddington EfW (Sutton, South London)
capacity_note: 26 MWe EfW; 382,000 t/yr waste
source: Viridor Beddington ERF website; Wikiwaste Beddington EfW; Letsrecycle.com EA permit expansion
notes: Serves South London Waste Partnership (Croydon, Kingston, Merton, Richmond, Sutton). 25-yr PPP contract signed Nov 2014. 2 lines, Martin Reverse Acting Grate. Operational Jan 2020. Capacity increased to 382,286 t/yr under EA permit variation.

name: Ferrybridge Multifuel 1 (FM1)
capacity_note: 68 MWe multifuel EfW; ~700,000 t/yr
source: Wikiwaste FM1; Global Energy Monitor Ferrybridge Multifuel 1; power-technology.com FM1 project; enfinium company website
notes: 68 MWe, commissioned 2015. Located on site of former Ferrybridge C coal power station, Knottingley, West Yorkshire. Adjacent to FM2. Combined FM1+FM2 capacity 1.35 Mt/yr — largest residual waste EfW site in UK. Former coal infrastructure and grid connection aids CCS viability.

name: Ferrybridge Multifuel 2 (FM2)
capacity_note: 67.8 MWe multifuel EfW; 566,000 t/yr
source: Wikiwaste FM2; Global Energy Monitor Ferrybridge Multifuel 2; Letsrecycle.com FM2 fully operational 2019
notes: 67.8 MWe, 566,000 t/yr, fully operational December 2019. Adjacent to FM1 on Ferrybridge site. Combined FM1+FM2 represents ~0.6 Mt biogenic CO2/yr — a top-tier UK cluster CCS opportunity.

name: Javelin Park EfW (Gloucestershire)
capacity_note: 17.4 MWe gross / 14.5 MWe net EfW; 190,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: Gloucestershire EfW; Wikiwaste Javelin Park EfW; Gloucestershire County Council; FCC Environment UK website
notes: 25-yr contract with Gloucestershire County Council (awarded Dec 2011). Fully operational January 2020. 190,000 t/yr; 17.4 MWe gross. FCC Servicios Medio Ambiente acquired Urbaser's UK affiliate June 2024 — now FCC Environment UK. Smaller plant, lower CCS priority.

name: Newhurst Energy Recovery Facility (Shepshed)
capacity_note: 42 MWe EfW; 350,000 t/yr waste
source: Encyclis press release full operations; Global Energy Monitor Newhurst ERF; Newhursterf.co.uk; HZI reference Newhurst; Biffa press release Jan 2022
notes: 42 MWe, 350,000 t/yr. Located near Shepshed, Leicestershire. Full operations commenced 2025 after 3-yr construction/commissioning. Operated by Encyclis. Kanadevia Inova (HZI) technology. UK East Midlands location — potential Humber CCS cluster linkage.

name: Protos Energy Recovery Facility (Cheshire)
capacity_note: 49.9 MWe EfW; 400,000 t/yr waste
source: Protos ERF website; Green Investment Group Financial Close press release 2020; Kanadevia Inova press release; Global Energy Monitor Protos EfW
notes: 49.9 MWe; 400,000 t/yr; within Protos strategic energy hub near Ellesmere Port. Commissioning phase 2024-2025. Encyclis acquired plant 2025. Kanadevia Inova green-lit to build UK's first full-scale carbon capture facility at Protos — making this a HIGH-priority BECCS site. HyNet proximity for CO2 transport.

name: Rookery South ERF (Stewartby, Bedfordshire)
capacity_note: 60+ MWe EfW; 545,000 t/yr waste
source: Covanta/Reworldwaste press release Jan 2022; Kanadevia Inova handover release; Global Energy Monitor Rookery South; Central Bedfordshire Council
notes: 60+ MWe; 545,000 t/yr. Located in former brickworks at Stewartby, Bedfordshire. Operational since January 2022. JV: Covanta/EQT 80%, Veolia 20%.

name: Earls Gate Energy Centre (Grangemouth, Scotland)
capacity_note: 22 MWe / 33 MWth EfW; 216,000 t/yr waste
source: EUWID Recycling; Earls Gate Energy Centre website; Green Investment Group 2018 announcement; Brockwell Energy project page
notes: 216,000 t/yr; 22 MWe. Fully operational June 2024 after delays. Scotland's first major EfW plant. Located in Grangemouth petrochemical/industrial cluster — potential Acorn CCS pathway (Caledonian Clean Energy project / St Fergus). Co-owned Encyclis/Brockwell; HZI operates.

name: Sysav Malmö Waste-to-Energy Plant
capacity_note: ~100 MWth district heat; 600,000 t/yr waste
source: Wikipedia: SYSAV waste-to-energy plant; NIB financing article; Waste Today; Friotherm case study (heat pump); Nordic Investment Bank
notes: Treats ~600,000 t/yr waste from southern Skåne province. Covers ~60% of Malmö district heating. Also known as Sjölunda facility. 2019 total waste received: 887,100 t; 1,464,700 MWh heat + 189,500 MWh electricity. Sweden has active CCS policy for WtE (LULUCF framework); Sysav is a leading candidate.

name: Renova Sävenäs WtE (Göteborg)
capacity_note: 42 MWe / ~400 MWth district heat; ~70 t/hr waste
source: Global Energy Monitor Sävenäs WtE; Renova facilities page; Smart City Sweden Renova profile; CTC-N Renova efficient waste recovery
notes: Annual production: 1,506 GWh district heat + 279 GWh electricity (2018). ~70 t/hr waste throughput. 60% of electricity labelled biofuel origin. Provides ~1/3 of Göteborg heat demand. Active CCS interest in Swedish WtE sector; Göteborg location near port infrastructure for CO2 shipping.

name: Filbornaverket WtE (Helsingborg)
capacity_note: 18 MWe / 72 MWth EfW CHP; 220,000 t/yr waste
source: Smart City Sweden Filborna CHP profile; CTC-N Filborna; Bioenergy International: Öresundskraft SEK 228M CCS grant; power-technology.com Helsingborg WtE profile
notes: 72 MWth / 18 MWe, 220,000 t/yr. Commissioned 2013. Supplies ~60% of Helsingborg district heating baseload. Öresundskraft secured SEK 228M Swedish Energy Agency grant for Filbornaverket CCS project — ACTIVE CCS development. Biogenic CO2 capture target ~100,000 t/yr.

name: Högdalen WtE (Stockholm)
capacity_note: ~200 MWth district heat; 700,000 t/yr waste capacity
source: Smart City Sweden: Waste incineration at Högdalenverket; Waste incineration in Nordic countries (Norden 2024); Stockholm Exergi corporate reports
notes: Stockholm Exergi also operates KVV8 (already in database). Högdalen is a separate WtE facility receiving ~700,000 t/yr capacity; multiple lines. Major biogenic CO2 source co-located with Stockholm Exergi's BECCS programme — strong CCS synergy.

name: Tammervoima WtE (Tampere, Finland)
capacity_note: 58.5 MWth / ~20 MWe EfW; 160,000 t/yr MSW
source: Tammervoima plant website; HZI Steinmüller reference Tampere; Valmet automation case study; Tampere waste-to-energy PDF 2018
notes: Operational since January 2016. 160,000 t/yr MSW; 310 GWh heat + 90 GWh electricity annually. Address: Hyötyvoimankuja 1, 33680 Tampere. Covers 15% of Tampere heating/electricity consumption. Separate from Naistenlahti biomass CHP (different facility).

name: Helen Vuosaari Bioenergy Plant (Helsinki)
capacity_note: 260 MWth biomass heat-only; forest chips
source: Helen press releases 2018, 2022; Bioenergy International 2019; Global Energy Monitor Vuosaari power station; e-architect Helsinki profile
notes: 260 MW forest-chip biomass heating plant; produces ~25% of Helsinki district heat. Heat-only (no electricity currently, CHP conversion technically feasible per Helen). Reduces Helsinki CO2 by ~700,000 t/yr vs coal. Commissioned Dec 2022 (full production). Helen targets carbon neutrality by 2030. CO2 estimated: calc from 260 MWth × ~8,000 hrs × ~0.2 tCO2/MWh_biomass.

name: Statkraft Heimdal WtE (Trondheim)
capacity_note: 40 MWth WtE; ~220,000 t/yr MSW
source: Industry About Trondheim Heimdal; Aker Carbon Capture pre-FEED press release; SLB Capturi; IEA Bioenergy full-scale WtE CCS in Norway (2025)
notes: Provides >30% of Trondheim municipal heating demand. Aker Carbon Capture (now SLB Capturi) awarded pre-FEED for CO2 capture at 220,000 t CO2/yr. Active BECCS/WtE-CCS development. Norway has strong CCS policy and Northern Lights CO2 storage infrastructure.

name: Fynsværket (Odense, Denmark)
capacity_note: 35 MWe / 85 MWth biomass CHP (Unit 8 straw); overall site ~421 MW
source: Wikipedia: Fyn Power Station; Global Energy Monitor Fyns power station; power-technology.com Fynsværket 8 profile; Bioenergy International Andritz EcoFluid 2021
notes: Fynsværket 8 (straw biomass): 35 MWe / 85 MWth. Straw from local farmers. Andritz EcoFluid biomass boiler (new Bio Blok 2 project). Remaining units converted to biomass/waste. Odense is Denmark's 3rd largest city. CO2 estimate covers straw-fired unit; total site biogenic CO2 larger.

name: Studstrupværket (Aarhus, Denmark)
capacity_note: 700 MWe biomass CHP (converted from coal 2016)
source: Wikipedia: Studstrup Power Station; Biomass Magazine 2016; State of Green; Canadian Biomass Magazine; Global Energy Monitor Studstrup
notes: One of the world's largest biomass CHP plants — 700 MWe converted from coal to wood pellets Oct 2016. District heating for ~106,000 homes; electricity for ~230,000 homes. Annual wood pellet consumption ~1.6 Mt. Saves ~310,000 t fossil CO2/yr. High-value BECCS target — biogenic CO2 ~1.8 Mt/yr estimated. Note: Ørsted Avedøre already in database, this is Studstrup separately.

name: Borregaard Sarpsborg (Biorefinery / Sulphite Pulp)
capacity_note: ~168,000 t/yr specialty cellulose; 1M solid m³/yr wood input; bioethanol + lignin + vanillin
source: Borregaard Wikipedia; ETIP Bioenergy factsheet Borregaard; Borregaard CDP 2023 climate change submission; Borregaard annual report 2023
notes: World's most advanced biorefinery — sulphite process (not kraft). Produces specialty cellulose, lignin biopolymers, bioethanol (20M L/yr), vanillin. EU ETS covered. Uses 94% of wood feedstock. High-concentration CO2 in recovery boiler flue gas. Norway's Northern Lights storage proximity makes CCS attractive. Not a standard kraft mill — distinct chemical signature.

name: Billerud Gruvön Mill (Grums, Sweden)
capacity_note: ~550,000 t/yr packaging board + market pulp; KM7 machine 550,000 t/yr
source: Billerud Gruvön mill page; Google Maps coordinates 59.3401, 13.1149; packaging-gateway.com Gruvön expansion; Billerud Annual & Sustainability Report 2022; ANDRITZ flue gas treatment 2023
notes: One of Europe's leading fluting/liner/liquid packaging board mills. ~30 km west of Karlstad, Värmland. New soda recovery boiler expanded capacity. Black liquor recovery boiler is dominant CO2 source (~75% of mill CO2). Billerud has active decarbonisation programme. New ANDRITZ flue gas precipitator for recovery boiler. CO2 estimated: calc from 550,000 t pulp × ~1.0 t biogenic CO2/t pulp (Frontiers 2026 European average).

name: Billerud Skärblacka Mill (Norrköping)
capacity_note: ~460,000 t/yr kraft paper (MG kraft, sack paper, fluting)
source: Billerud Skärblacka mill page; Wikipedia: Billerud; euwid-paper.com PM10 startup; Billerud production units overview
notes: Specialises in white MG/MF kraft paper, brown sack paper, fluting. 460,000 t/yr. Located just outside Norrköping, Östergötland. PM10 paper machine started. Two laboratories for food and medical packaging R&D. CO2 estimate: calc from 460,000 t × ~1.0 tCO2/t.

name: Billerud Frövi/Rockhammar Mill
capacity_note: ~500,000 t/yr cartonboard + liquid packaging board
source: Billerud Frövi/Rockhammar mill page; Billerud Wikipedia; euwid-paper.com Frövi SP4 recovery boiler 2023 (SEK 2.6B investment)
notes: ~30 km north of Örebro, Västmanland. Produces cartonboard for luxury/consumer goods and liquid packaging. New SP4 recovery boiler inaugurated Sep 2023 (SEK 2.6B). Expanded pulp capacity enables higher CO2 capture potential. CO2 estimated: calc 500,000 t × ~1.0 tCO2/t.

name: SCA Obbola Mill (Umeå)
capacity_note: 725,000 t/yr kraftliner; world's largest kraftliner machine
source: SCA Obbola mill page; PULPAPERnews: world's largest kraftliner machine 2023; AFRY project page; Valmet lime kiln reference SCA Obbola
notes: Integrated kraftliner mill just outside Umeå, Västerbotten. New world's largest kraftliner machine commissioned 2023. 100% fossil-free lime kiln (Valmet). Baltic Sea deep-water harbour. ~725,000 t/yr production — generates very large biogenic CO2 stream from recovery boiler. High CCS retrofit attractiveness.

name: SCA Munksund Mill (Piteå)
capacity_note: 410,000 t/yr kraft paper (white + brown packaging paper)
source: SCA Munksund page; SCA Munksund expansion packaging-gateway.com; Valmet fossil-free lime kiln reference SCA Munksund
notes: 410,000 t/yr white/brown kraft packaging paper. Located in Piteå, Norrbotten. Adjacent to Smurfit Kappa Piteå — potential shared CCS infrastructure in Piteå port area. Valmet delivered fossil-free lime kiln. Uses spruce/pine from sustainably managed forests in Northern Sweden.

name: Smurfit Westrock Piteå (Kraftliner Mill)
capacity_note: 700,000 t/yr kraftliner (Europe's largest); sulphate mill with 3 pulp lines + 2 PMs
source: Smurfit Kappa Piteå mill page; Wikidata Q47156448 coordinates 65°18'55.8N 21°26'40E; Wagenborg case study; Valmet rebuild 2019; packaging-gateway.com upgrades
notes: Europe's largest kraftliner producer; 700,000 t/yr. Mill at Kolugnsvägen 30, 941 86 Piteå. Two softwood pulp lines, one hardwood line with bleach plant, recycled fibre line, two PMs. 90% exported. Active sustainability drive (combustion/cooking upgrades). Piteå port enables CO2 shipping. ~510 employees.

name: Holmen Braviken Paper Mill (Norrköping)
capacity_note: 605,000 t/yr newsprint/SC paper (mechanical pulp); 2 paper machines
source: Holmen Braviken mill page; Wikipedia: Braviken Paper Mill; Andritz rebuild completion June 2025; Valmet wash press 2023
notes: 605,000 t/yr printing/writing paper on Bråviken bay, outside Norrköping. 100% fresh wood fibre. Two PMs. Deepwater harbour. Mechanical pulp process (TMP) — lower biogenic CO2 per tonne than kraft mills (no recovery boiler), but large scale still significant. CO2 estimate is lower per tonne (~0.5 tCO2/t vs ~1.0 for kraft). Recently rebuilt PM for efficiency and flexibility (ANDRITZ June 2025).

name: Holmen Iggesund Mill (Iggesund, Sweden)
capacity_note: ~200,000 t/yr premium paperboard (Invercote); integrated chemical pulp mill
source: Holmen Iggesund mill page; iggesund.com about/locations; Wikipedia: Holmen Iggesund; euwid-paper.com cartonboard expansion 2023
notes: World-class kraft-based premium paperboard mill (Invercote) dating to 1685. Located on Hälsingland coast, Baltic Sea. ~200,000 t/yr premium board. Integrated bleached kraft pulp mill with recovery boiler. Holmen has active low-carbon agenda. Baltic Sea location enables CO2 ship transport.

name: UPM Kaukas Pulp Mill (Lappeenranta)
capacity_note: 700,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp (two lines)
source: UPM Pulp Kaukas page; UPM press release Kaukas investment; UPM global operations map entry; Wikimapia Kaukas paper mill
notes: On shore of Lake Saimaa, Lappeenranta, SE Finland. Integrated site: pulp mill + magazine paper mill + sawmill + UPM Lappeenranta biorefinery (HVO diesel). 700,000 t/yr two-line kraft mill. Recovery boiler generates dominant biogenic CO2 stream. UPM committed to carbon neutrality — CCS interest rising.

name: UPM Kymi Pulp Mill (Kouvola)
capacity_note: 870,000 t/yr bleached softwood + birch kraft pulp (expanded 2016)
source: UPM Pulp Kymi page; UPM press release Kymi expansion Jan 2016; GlobeNewswire Kymi opening; ANDRITZ pulp drying world record
notes: 870,000 t/yr (expanded 2016; €160M investment). Located in Kuusankoski, Kouvola along River Kymi, SE Finland. Integrated with paper mill. ANDRITZ pulp drying plant achieved world record throughput. One of the largest single-site kraft pulp mills in Europe — major biogenic CO2 point source. UPM temporarily curtailed production Aug 2024 (market conditions).

name: UPM Pietarsaari Pulp Mill (Jakobstad)
capacity_note: 800,000 t/yr bleached softwood + birch kraft pulp
source: UPM Pulp Pietarsaari page; UPM biochemicals global operations map (location 87); UPM ABB reference story
notes: Gulf of Bothnia, western Finland (Jakobstad/Pietarsaari). 800,000 t/yr — co-located with Alholma sawmill and Alholmens Kraft power plant (already in database). Integrated industrial cluster. Softwood and birch pulp. Recovery boiler generates large concentrated biogenic CO2 stream ideal for CCS.

name: Stora Enso Oulu Mill
capacity_note: 750,000 t/yr consumer board + kraftliner + softwood pulp (by 2027)
source: Stora Enso Oulu mill page; packaging-gateway.com Oulu new board line; Packaging Europe €1.1B investment article; Stora Enso press release Aug 2025 inauguration; ANDRITZ Stora Enso Oulu
notes: Deep-sea harbour at Oulu, northern Finland. €1.1B investment in consumer packaging board line (inaugurated Aug 2025). Target 750,000 t/yr by 2027 (folding boxboard + kraftliner + softwood pulp). 90% CO2 reduction claimed for new board line vs old coal process. Large recovery boiler remains dominant biogenic CO2 source.

name: Stora Enso Imatra Mills (Kaukopää + Tainionkoski)
capacity_note: ~1,000,000 t/yr consumer packaging board + pulp (combined two units)
source: Stora Enso Imatra mill page; Paper360 May 2019; Stora Enso Wikipedia; Wikimapia Stora Enso Imatra Paper Mill; coords ~61.249, 28.857 (Imatra city)
notes: Two integrated production units (Kaukopää + Tainionkoski) in Imatra, E Finland near Russian border. ~1 Mt/yr liquid packaging board and consumer packaging board. One of the world's largest LPB producers. 90%+ exported. Two recovery boilers — large concentrated biogenic CO2 point source.

name: Stora Enso Sunila Mill (Kotka)
capacity_note: 370,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp; lignin extraction biorefinery
source: Stora Enso Sunila mill investment press release 2013; IEA Bioenergy Sunila biorefinery; Stora Enso Wikipedia; bioenergy-news.com Sunila
notes: 370,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp. Located at Sunila, near Kotka, S Finland. €32M biorefinery investment to extract lignin from black liquor — replaces up to 90% of natural gas with lignin. Lignin extraction reduces recovery boiler load slightly but still major biogenic CO2 source.

name: Metsä Fibre Rauma Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 650,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp (Metsä Strong brand)
source: Metsä Fibre Rauma mill page; paperage.com Joutseno restart Dec 2025; metsagroup.com pulp production overview
notes: ECF bleached softwood pulp (Metsä Strong); 650,000 t/yr. Produces biochemicals and bioenergy alongside pulp. Rauma port enables CO2 ship export. One of four Metsä Fibre Finnish mills. Production temporarily curtailed 2025 (market conditions) but core asset.

name: Metsä Fibre Joutseno Pulp Mill
capacity_note: 690,000 t/yr bleached softwood kraft pulp
source: Metsä Fibre Joutseno mill page; paperage.com Joutseno restart Dec 2025; coordinates: Haukilahdentie 27, Joutseno ~61.118, 28.502
notes: 690,000 t/yr. Located in Joutseno (Lappeenranta municipality), SE Finland on Lake Saimaa shores, 20 km N of Lappeenranta. Restarted Dec 2025 after temporary shutdown. Co-located with Metsä Board BCTMP mill. Recovery boiler dominant biogenic CO2 source.
